experiment: Bidirectional state-token activation interchange for PoL2 contract variables

design.checkpoint: Kev 0.8B + matched PoL2-contract SFT and task-only LoRA arms; three existing seeds per arm
design.intervention: exchange only residual activations overlapping the changed trusted-field value token(s), at all transformer blocks
controls: same clause value with a later alternate request as causal-position placebo
design.comparison: task_only is a matched SFT objective control; both arms use the same base, state pairs, seeds, and evaluation procedure
design.primary_metric: target-action logit minus logsumexp of the other three candidate logits
design.unit: seed x one exact one-field minimal pair per contract factor; exploratory mechanistic diagnostic
limitations: The tested contract is a narrow synthetic operationalization, not complete PoL2.
Activation exchange at the state boundary does not establish a unique or complete internal algorithm.
The same deterministic contract generated supervision and test targets.
Three seeds and one canonical pair per factor do not support population-level inference.
The result is evidence about this model, checkpoint, and specific intervention distribution only.
